version.changelog:
Version 1.0.3

- Rebranded skill from "ragflow-knowledge" to "ragflow-dataset-ingest" and updated naming conventions.
- Removed redundant or excessive procedural and security policy documentation.
- Added clear bilingual (English/Chinese) trigger phrase lists for each supported intent (dataset/document management, parsing, retrieval, model listing).
- Clarified and streamlined the supported workflow for invoking scripts and handling user requests.
- Removed the readme.md file.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ragflow-skill
Version: 1.0.3

The ragflow-skill bundle is a legitimate set of tools designed to interface with the RAGFlow API for dataset management, document ingestion, and knowledge retrieval. The scripts (e.g., `datasets.py`, `upload.py`, `search.py`) use standard Python libraries like `urllib` for network requests and `argparse` for command-line interaction. Security controls are present, such as restricting environment variable loading in `common.py` to specific RAGFLOW-prefixed keys. The instructions in `SKILL.md` are well-scoped to the intended functionality and include safety requirements like user confirmation for deletion operations. No evidence of malicious intent, obfuscation, or unauthorized data exfiltration was found.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a coherent RAGFlow client (creates/uploads/parses/searches datasets) but packaging metadata and runtime expectations don't fully match and the skill will read local files and require a bearer API key and base URL — review before installing and only point it at a trusted server.

dimensions.detail: The name, description, SKILL.md and bundled scripts all align: this is a client for managing RAGFlow datasets/documents and performing searches. However the registry-level metadata reported no required env vars while the included agents/openai.yaml and the scripts (require_api_key/resolve_base_url) clearly expect RAGFLOW_API_URL and RAGFLOW_API_KEY. That metadata mismatch is an inconsistency to be aware of.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions restrict the agent to using the bundled scripts and explicitly describe workflows (create/list/upload/parse/search) and a deletion confirmation flow. The scripts legitimately read local file paths for uploads and allow json/@file inputs for update operations — this is expected for an ingest client but means the skill will read local files you point it at.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only skill) and bundled scripts are included. No external downloads or package installs are requested, so install risk is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a RAGFlow base URL and a bearer API key at runtime (agents/openai.yaml and scripts call require_api_key/resolve_base_url). That is proportionate to a remote client; however the registry metadata omitted these required env vars which is an inconsistency. Also the skill will POST file contents and metadata to the configured base URL — ensure the RAGFLOW_API_URL points to a trusted server and the API key scope is minimal.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always: true, is user-invocable, and does not request system-wide config changes. It does read repo/env config via load_repo_env (likely to discover variables) but does not appear to modify other skills or request elevated persistent privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is a client for a RAGFlow server and will read files you point it at and send them to the configured server. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the required environment variables (RAGFLOW_API_URL and RAGFLOW_API_KEY) — the registry metadata omitted them but the code requires them. 2) Only set RAGFLOW_API_URL to a server you trust; uploaded files and document contents will be transmitted there. 3) Review common.py (require_api_key, load_repo_env, resolve_base_url) to understand where credentials come from and whether any repo config files are read. 4) Be cautious with local file paths and @path JSON flags — they allow the script to read arbitrary local files. 5) Note a minor code anomaly in a truncated script (parse_status.py ends unusually in the provided snippet) — run tests or inspect scripts locally before granting runtime access. If you cannot verify the server and env handling, avoid installing or run the scripts in an isolated environment with least privilege.
